description:
The /fly HUD speed readout (labelled Velocity with a vis-viva chip) shows 'NaN km/s' for the entire transit to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and presumably Ceres/Vesta/Psyche/Bennu). The same NaN propagates through the 3D velocity-arrow length and the ".toFixed(2)" call on the SpacecraftInfoCard prop.

Expected: The HUD should display a physically meaningful positive speed in km/s throughout the transit. For a Hohmann transfer to Jupiter, the speed should start at ~38–40 km/s at Earth departure (perihelion) and decrease to ~7–8 km/s at Jupiter arrival (aphelion), following the vis-viva equation: v = √(µ · (2/r − 1/a)) where a = (R_EARTH_AU + R_DEST_AU) / 2, not a = (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2.

Acceptance criteria:
- The HUD speed readout must never display 'NaN' for any mission that /fly can load. Number.isNaN(heliocentricKms) must be false on every frame of every transit. [code-invariant: NaN is a crash in the user-facing display — no document needed to assert the app must not display 'NaN km/s'.]
- The transfer semi-major axis aTransferAu passed to heliocentricSpeed() must be derived from the actual destination's orbital radius for non-Moon missions, not hardcoded to Mars. Expected: a = (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2 for outer destinations. [repo-data: DESTINATIONS constant at src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts:98-120 — contains a (semi-major axis) for every DestinationId including jupiter (5.203 AU), saturn (9.537 AU), uranus (19.191 AU), neptune (30.069 AU), pluto. The hardcoded (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU)/2 ≈ 1.262 AU at src/routes/fly/+page.svelte:952 is factually wrong for any destination other than Mars.]
- The speed readout value must satisfy the vis-viva equation bounds for the actual destination: for Jupiter, at Earth departure (r=1.0 AU) with a=(1+5.203)/2=3.102 AU, v ≈ 38.5 km/s; at Jupiter arrival the value should decrease monotonically. For all outer planets, the value must be finite and positive across the full [R_EARTH_AU, R_DEST_AU] distance range. [spec: ADR-030 §'Trajectory math' / fly-physics.ts:L35-41 — vis-viva is the canonical formula. The function itself is sound; the call site feeds it the wrong transfer a.]

Domain facts:
- Jupiter semi-major axis: 5.203 AU (from static/data/planets.json)
- Saturn semi-major axis: 9.537 AU
- Uranus semi-major axis: 19.191 AU
- Neptune semi-major axis: 30.069 AU
- Mars semi-major axis: 1.524 AU (the value currently hardcoded into the speed call site)

Target: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — line 952 — $derived expression for heliocentricKms
